newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PGM export delay due to govt changes-C.Bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia PGM export delay due to govt changes-C.Bank.

text.p: Russia's slowness in signing a decree that would free up long-delayed palladium exports to Japan was due to recent changes in the government, a Central Bank spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

"The absence of a government decree on export quotas, which was meant to have been signed some time in the first quarter of this year, is because of the arrival of a new government," Central Bank deputy press director Natalya Khomenko told Reuters.
President Boris Yeltsin announced sweeping changes to the leadership last month, with the new team spearheaded by first deputy premiers Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov.
But the government has had its hands full with urgent monetary and social problems at home.
Khomenko said the delays were not connected with any disagreement between the Central Bank and the Finance Ministry over who should control precious metals exports, as some market talk has suggested.
"There is no disagreement between the Central Bank and the Finance Ministry, which looks after Almazjuvelirexport," Khomenko said.
Almazjuvelirexport is the state export agency that carries out deliveries as stipulated in the government document.

She did not say when she expected the decree on platinum group metal exports to be signed, bu added that the Central Bank had received assurances from the government that the decree would be signed soon.
"The government has a lot of very important tasks, and the government has said to us to wait, and that it will do this very soon," Khomenko said.

Vladimir Rybkin, head of the Finance Ministry's precious metals and stones section said last week he expected the decree would be signed some time this week, and that Russian deliveries could re-start as early as May.
But on Wednesday he said he could not be sure this would happen.
"Last week that was an estimate, but at the moment I can't say anything about this," Rybkin said.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of palladium and Russia the largest producer of the metal.
Contract talks are usually held in December for deliveries to begin in the next calendar year.
Palladium prices soared to 21-month highs last week on concerns over protracted delays to Russian deliveries to Japan, but have since lost some of the gains.
